reason: The cited evidence does not address Q235 steel, its annealing, or oxide film formation on low-alloy steels. E1 describes protective oxide layers on Cr/Al/Si-containing alloys in different environments, E2 discusses phase instability in a Cr-Mn-Fe-Ni HEA, and E3 examines passivation of CoCrFeNiTix HEAs in NaCl. None of these support the specific premises about annealing-induced Mn/Si-enriched oxide films on Q235 steel or their barrier performance under the proposed conditions.
premises: Annealing Q235 steel at ~700 °C in low-oxygen forms a thin, uniform oxide film enriched in Mn and Si
This engineered oxide film acts as an effective barrier against corrosive salt environments
Film integrity (adherent, non-porous) retards corrosion under cyclic room- and high-temperature conditions
Film degradation (spallation, porosity) leads to accelerated corrosion
The protective mechanism is analogous to Cr2O3, Al2O3, or SiO2 barrier layers on alloys
